pieces.content:
Thanks for coming and
you made it
You made to the Volvelle Social Club
It’s our annual meeting
and thanks for coming

We are moving devices yet
clubs of five are outlawed.
Everyone signs up in a round-robin
and we can’t have a pentagram
So no clubs of five

It’s hot today
Really hot inside
It feels about 72 degrees
Not very good weather
for an annual meeting.

But let’s press on
The heat of our bodies
has made things worse
(The heat) Let’s start.
Add a disc to the Volvelle.

An ionic column and
our volunteers and
partners are energetic. You
look so well I hardly believe it
Like an ionic column

Dearest members note
we begin the program
very energetically.
You can change your mind
If you want you can

When the fifth person joins
You go into hibernation.
It’s imperative that
you sleep until the next
Interested person is found.

At first this was painful
But it’s adventure really
All five of you there and
a sleeping adventure
and not Convening

You will be fine but
things don’t look good though.
It’s sort-of stuck between two.
Just rattle the pin and
Add a disc to the Volvelle please

parent.content:
A new format of love is the bringing-over of a grey t-shirt to be stashed in the other’s place. The generation that this applies to don’t so much agree to the particular supplier and instance of shirt as much have it decided for them through convention and availability. Most poisons are produced for a particular use. When you wear the grey t-shirt, you look like an ionic column. But you shouldn't wear the shirt; that would reduce the situation unbearably; that would suck out the idea. Instead rest something unbending on the shirt while you’re cleaning up — other shirts, say, or a phone.

Having the t-shirt stashed promises you an internal market. It sits off just to the side and people do things to it, which creates a form to make sense of the varieties of encounter that relate to you. Keep it by your bedside. You can think about it at work.
